what_changed:
No revision is committed. The steer says that if the evidence still shows the baseline doing this unprompted, the branch goes back to main. NOT DONE: the permission system denied the `git reset --hard main` command, so I did not retry it. Branch test/eval-redesign-executing-verify still points at ee2e5919, the designer's V4 commit, and the orchestrator or user has to reset it. package-lock.json is still dirty and uncommitted, as instructed.

Each finding, checked against the gitignored pool by replaying every transcript in Python over tool blocks only, with NUL bytes stripped:

(1) CEILING (blocker): holds, and I reproduced it exactly. With v4's A1 logic applied to T2 and README.md, 26 of 37 baselines mark T2 `[~]` before the first README write: 144454 3/3, 150148 2/3, 151252 9/10, 023755 1/3, 042247 2/5, 061059 6/10, 105529 3/3. The baselines also say it in their own words, for example "Now T2 — marking in-progress first, then writing the example" (061059 b1), "marking in-progress before touching README" (144454 t3), "Marking T2 in-progress before I touch anything — the checklist is the only state" (150148 t1).

(2) LEAK (the Context clause "box can be reclaimed"): holds. But removing it does not create the headroom the design needs. Of the 26 baselines that claimed T2, at most 14 mention a crash, reclaim, kill or the box anywhere in their prose. That is an upper bound, because the regex also counts a false hit like "this box can't reach". So at least 12 of 37 baselines (32%) claimed without citing the clause. Several cited the banner ("this file is the only state") instead, and the banner is the format contract, so it stays. The resume-after-an-unwarned-stop premise also stays, because it is the scenario.

(3) T2 PRIMING: holds as a confound. Removing T2's `[!]` would make the CHANGELOG task the first task with real work, which is exactly the position T2 held. So T2's 70% rate (100% on the current model, 105529) is the best available proxy for the revised design, not a reason to expect a lower one. 105529 trial-1 claims selectively: one sed sets T3 (no work) to `[x]` and T2 (real work) to `[~]`. That is a choice about which task has work, not a side effect of the forced edit.

(4) Bash write detection: holds. I tested the committed regex: `cat > CHANGELOG.md` matches. `cat > /private/tmp/x/CHANGELOG.md`, `> "$PWD/CHANGELOG.md"` and `cp /tmp/c CHANGELOG.md` do not, so a write-then-mark run would fall through to the mark-anywhere fallback. This is moot under no-spend.

(5) Header saying 29/31 where the Design Notes say 37/23: holds. My recount matches the Design Notes. Also moot.

(6) The note about MARK_RE false negatives is accepted as a low risk and is moot.

Why no revision was committed: the A/B runs at k=5 (D-049). I computed `ciForDelta` with treatment at 5/5. Baseline 0/5 gives a lower bound of 1.00, 1/5 gives 0.24, 2/5 gives -0.08 and 3/5 gives -0.28. So IMPROVED needs a baseline at or below 1/5. Take the optimistic assumption that removing the leak eliminates every baseline claim that cites the box. The floor rate is then still about 0.32, and P(baseline ≤ 1/5) ≈ 0.49. That assumes a perfect treatment and three preflight sessions spent first. The pool does not support predicting a discriminating result, so a further edit would manufacture a gap rather than measure one.
baseline_expectation: I expect a no-skill baseline to mark the CHANGELOG task `[~]` before writing CHANGELOG.md in most trials, roughly 50–100%, even with the reclaim clause removed and T2's `[!]` removed. The evidence comes from the recorded pool on this Setup. On T2, the only task in the fixture that needed real work, 26 of 37 baselines claimed `[~]` before the first README write. The current-model preflight (20260930-105529) did it 3/3, silently, with selective claiming: T3 went straight to `[x]` while T2 got `[~]`. At least 12 of the 26 never mention a crash, reclaim or the box. Several give the banner's "this file is the only state" as their reason, and the banner is the format contract, so it stays. Under the k=3 preflight that predicts a likely BLOCK. Even if it passes, a k=5 A/B needs a baseline at or below 1/5 to read IMPROVED.

finding_for_decision_log: On eval-executing-verify-decides-done, the baseline already marks a task that needs real work `[~]` before doing it. That happened in 26 of 37 recorded baseline trials on T2, 3/3 on the current model in 20260930-105529, often in prose like "marking in-progress first, then writing the example", and in at least 12 trials without citing the reclaimable-box Context. So executing's "Mark it `[~]`" step (§Running a task step 1, plus the Unattended paragraph) formalizes behavior the model already shows, and V4 was not spent on a preflight. The standing coverage for this skill is the 6.1.1 BLOCK plus the earlier pre-repair +0.40, recorded as unmet-but-covered. A future scenario should measure a different executing claim, such as the never-`[x]`-without-reading-verify rule or the attended checkpoint, rather than re-roll this one.
